deck.title: NES — 8-bit design system for the web

props.title:
==NES==
A design system with a cheat code for charm.
props.subtitle: Chunky pixels, a strict palette, and interfaces that feel like a game — bottled as real, reusable components.

slides.notes: Open with the hook: modern web design got clean to the point of sterile. NES is the cheat code — real engineering with the flavour of the 8-bit era.

props.title: Modern UI got sterile. The NES era had flavour.

left.label: NOW
left.title: Clean to a fault
points: Rounded corners, soft greys, safe whitespace
Every product looks like every other product

right.label: NES ERA
right.title: Interfaces that felt like a game
points: Chunky pixels and hard offset shadows
A strict palette you could name on sight
Every screen felt like pressing START

slides.notes: Contrast the sterile present with the flavour of 8-bit. The punchline: NES bottles that flavour as actual web components, not a screenshot of nostalgia.

tiles.title: Press Start 2P
tiles.body: Display type straight from the cartridge label — pixel-perfect at every size.

tiles.title: #209cee on #212529
tiles.body: The classic NES blue over near-black. A palette strict enough to be a brand.

tiles.title: 4px pixel edges
tiles.body: Hard corners and offset shadows — no blur, no softness, all signal.

tiles.title: Buttons, tags, cards, pagination
tiles.body: The everyday kit of a web UI, each piece dressed in full 8-bit.

slides.notes: Walk the four ingredients: type, palette, borders, components. Everything else in the system is built from these.

props.label: PROVEN IN THE WILD
props.title: One live Tumblr blog, themed end to end.
props.body: Every post type — text, photo, quote, link, chat, audio, video, answers — rendered in full 8-bit dress. Not a mock-up: a production blog running on the system today.

slides.notes: Proof beats promises. The Tumblr theme exercises every post type the platform has — the system holds up across all of them.

props.kicker: WHY A SYSTEM, NOT A ONE-OFF THEME
props.title: Tokens and components. The next site gets the look in ==hours==, consistently.
props.body: Nostalgia with engineering discipline: change a token, the whole world reskins.

slides.notes: The thesis of the project. A one-off theme is a souvenir; a system is a tool. Tokens and components make the second site cheap and the tenth one trivial.

items.title: Pixel components
items.body: Buttons, inputs, cards, tags, pagination — the full everyday kit, 8-bit to the last pixel.

items.title: Design tokens
items.body: Palette, type, and spacing as variables. Retheme the world by changing a handful of values.

items.title: Strict palette
items.body: NES blue on near-black, WCAG AA contrast throughout — charm that never costs readability.

items.title: Open source
items.body: MIT-spirited and public on GitHub. Fork it, theme with it, ship it.

slides.notes: Four pillars: the component kit, the token layer, the accessible strict palette, and open source. Keep it quick.
